### Observed differences

- In the later window, A10 appears in about 62% of traces (up from about 22%), with mean occurrences per trace rising from 0.24 to 0.65. Its position shifted earlier: the median relative position moved from about 0.55 to 0.23. [OCC003, POS001]
- A10 now often directly follows A15 (A15→A10 increased from about 2% to 36% of A15's outgoing transitions), and A10 now leads to A16 in about 91% of its outgoing transitions (up from 13%). [DIR003, DIR002]
- A10 now co-occurs with A16, A27, A28, A29, A30, A42, A47 and A48 in about 62% of traces (up from 22%), and in most of those it appears before them. [REL002, REL007-013]
- Activities A19, A20, A25 and A26 almost disappeared: participation dropped from about 26%, 26%, 24% and 25% to 2.5%, 1.5%, 1% and 1% respectively. [OCC004-007]
- A04 and A06 also decreased from about 17% to 5% and 6% respectively. [OCC001, OCC002]
- The outgoing transitions of A28 and A29 now go almost exclusively to A29 and A30 respectively, whereas before they also went to A19, A20, A25 and A26. [DIR008, DIR009]
- The branch containing A19, A20, A25 and A26 no longer co-occurs with A10 or with each other; instead, those activities are absent. [REL003-006, REL022-024, REL032-033]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the process changed so that A10 is now a frequent early step, and a branch involving A19, A20, A25 and A26 (and possibly A04 and A06) is no longer executed. The changes are consistent across occurrence, routing, co-occurrence and position indicators. A competing explanation of sampling differences in variant frequencies is unlikely given the large and consistent shifts, though the disappearance of A19, A20, A25 and A26 is based on only a few traces in the later window. [OCC003, OCC004-007, DIR002, DIR003, REL001-013, POS001]
